newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends down after two-way trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends down after two-way trade.

text.p: Hong Kong spot gold ended a shade down on Wednesday compared to New York's previous close after busy two-way trade and strong support from physical demand, bullion dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$340.10/60 an ounce on Wednesday against New York's US$340.30/80 close on Tuesday.
"The gold price kept moving, we couldn't guess which direction it would head for next," said one gold dealer.
Sources reported buying from Japan's Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) on a weaker dollar, matched by fund selling.
Physical demand was said healthy, although some dealers said Hong Kong was not as active as other players in the region, such as India.
Local gold ended HK$25 lower at HK$3,152 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society dropped to -5.00 from +7.00.
